title: The three-component-intersection extremal conjecture for odd n
source: Imre Leader, Žarko Ranđelović and Ta Sheng Tan, “A Note on Hamiltonian-Intersecting Families of Graphs”, arXiv:2309.00757 (2023). (https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.00757), Conjecture 7

significance.root_decision: For every h >= 1, on n = 6h-1 labelled vertices there is a family of (1+6h+12h^2)*2^(C(n,2)-6h) graphs whose pairwise intersections all have at most three components, exceeding the conjectured bound ((n+3)^2/8)*2^(C(n,2)-n); the ratio tends to 4/3. The family consists of all graphs missing at most one edge from each of at most two of the three paths of a spanning theta graph. At n = 5 it has 304 graphs against a bound of 256. Lean proves the family for all h, failure above every order threshold, and the literal negation.
significance.caveat: The Discrete Mathematics journal version of the source is unread (publisher refuses automated access). The conjecture was restated unchanged in Randelovic 2025 Cambridge thesis.

root_basis: Root extracted the five modules from the appendix into an empty directory, rebuilt and kernel-checked them (all exit 0, object hashes identical to the author build, axioms exactly the allowed three), read the definitions Valid, bound, compCount and Conjecture and the three endpoint statements against the source statement quoted by the reviewer, and read and checked the written proof (pair validity cases, the count (m+1)^3-m^3, the bound comparison).
